introText: Device Reminder detects when household devices start and finish and notifies you.
placeholderText: This section is configured in a later step.
recipientsHelp: Recipients receive the device messages. Assign them per device. Active-from/until limit the time window (do not disturb).
pollIntervalHelp: 1 to 600 seconds. Count-based thresholds (start/end count) count ticks of this interval.
dev_sourceInfo: Select the socket, device or alias the device is connected to. The power and switch states are detected automatically. Choose manual entry to enter the states yourself.
dev_hintNotFound: No power state was found for this source. Enter the power state manually.
dev_hintNoPattern: The source was not recognized as a socket. A single power state was used; please check it and add a switch state if needed.
dev_abortHelp: Report when the device is switched off before the run has finished.
dev_autoOffHelp: Switches the socket off after the delay below.
dev_reminderHelp: Repeats the end message until it is acknowledged.
dev_reminderAckStateHelp: Any state that changes to true acknowledges the device.
dev_abortFixedHelp: Corrects the abort detection of version 3.1.2. An abort is only reported when the switch of the device is off, so a switch must be configured. Leave off to keep the old behavior.
devicesHelp: Add, edit and operate your devices here. The same list is available in the Config Manager tab of the instance.
dm_learnInfo: The power curve was analysed. Check the values; saving writes them into the device (no restart).
rcp_volumeHelp: The volume is set for the announcement and restored afterwards.
rcp_volumeStateIdHelp: Only needed if the volume state is not found automatically (e.g. Alexa groups). Normally leave empty.
rcp_targetHelp: Choose a user or chat known to the telegram instance.
rcp_windowHelp: Messages are only sent in this time window (also across midnight). Empty = always.
rcp_priorityHelp: Priority of the target service (Pushover: -2 to 2, 2 = needs confirmation).
rcp_topicHelp: ntfy topic the message is published to.
rcp_discordHelp: Fill in at least the user name, user ID or channel ID.
rcp_messengerHelp: All installed instances of the supported messenger adapters.
rcp_echoHelp: Echo devices and groups of the chosen alexa2 instance.
rcp_testHelp: Sends a test message with the settings shown here (also before saving).
dev_enumsHelp: Assigns the device to rooms and functions (categories). Needed, for example, to show it in the Devices tab.
dm_learnSourceInfo: The power state of this device is stored by a history adapter. The adapter can derive the detection values from all runs of the last 30 days instead of recording a new run.
dm_learnEvalInfo: Every run was replayed with each detection mode: runs detected correctly / runs found · mean (max) time until the end is reported. The recommended mode is preselected. Cross-check: runs that would also have been detected if that run had been missing from the history; if it is lower, learn again after more runs.
dm_learnPauseInfo: Pause protection: a long pause (e.g. soaking) only counts as the end after the hold time, so every other run reports the end quickly. 0 = off.
typeTrailerBurstTooltip: Longest drum movement after the programme in s (15-180). 0 = anti-crease filter off (3.1.2 behaviour).
typeTrailerGapTooltip: Minimum quiet time before a drum movement in s. 0 = 3 polls, at least 30 s. Shorter stops (tumbling while washing) are never held.
typeTrailerAfterTooltip: Drum movements are held only this many seconds after the start. 0 = unused.
typeTrailerBlockTooltip: Drum movements are held only after a block of at least 2 minutes whose power in its last 2 minutes is at least this value (e.g. spinning at the end). 0 = unused.
typeTrailerMaxTooltip: Length of the anti-crease phase after the end in s (900-14400, default 7200). It also ends after 20 minutes without a drum movement.
dm_autoOptimizeHelp: After every run the detection is checked against all stored runs and improved without restarting the instance. Off = the base values of the device.
dm_optimizeNotifyHelp: Every change of the automatic optimisation is also sent to the recipients of the device.
dm_optStatus_drift: Drift: no automatic tightening, repairs go on
dm_optTrailer_notSeparable: Not separable, end after the anti-crease phase
dm_optKind_finalSuspend: Final phase suspended (wrong early end found)
dm_optReset: Reset to the base values of the device
dm_optClearConfirm: Delete all stored runs and optimised values of this device? Your decisions about runs are kept unless you tick the box.
dm_optAdopt: Adopt the values in use as base values of the device
dm_optInfo: The detection is checked after every run against all stored runs of all programmes. Repairs follow after one faulty run, tightenings only after at least 8 runs and 24 hours.
dm_learnTrailerInfo: Anti-crease filter: drum movements after the programme are ignored, so the end is reported when the programme finishes. 0 = off.
dm_learnTrailerNotSeparable: An anti-crease phase was found, but a phase inside a programme looks the same. The end is only reported after the anti-crease phase (never too early).
valuesInDeviceHelp: The detection values (thresholds, mode, pause protection, anti-crease protection, final phase) are stored in each device. Choose them when you add a device (template, old template or another device) and change them in the Device Manager with "Edit". Learned values are saved there as well. Old device types of an earlier version stay available as templates until you remove them with the instance action "Remove old templates".
dev_sourceValuesHelp: Template, old template of an earlier version or another device. Copying from a device takes only the start and end values and the pause and anti-crease protection; the final phase and the phases are learned at the new device.
dm_copyFinalHint: The final phase and the phases are not copied. Learn them at the new device.
dm_removeArchiveConfirm: Remove the old templates (device types of an earlier version) from the instance? The devices stay unchanged. The instance restarts.
finalMinValTooltip: Power at or above which a block counts as the final band of the programme (e.g. the last spin). 0 = final phase off. Works only together with "time in band".
finalMinSecTooltip: Time the power has to stay in the final band before a pause can count as an early end. 0 = final phase off.
finalMaxValTooltip: A value at or above this discards the block. 0 = open.
finalHotValTooltip: Power at or above which a new run is assumed after an early end. 0 = off. Usually set by learning.
finalAfterSecTooltip: The final block counts only this long after the start of the run. 0 = no condition.
finalQuietSecTooltip: Time below the lower edge after a qualified block until the run counts as finished early. 0 = 120 s.
finalDipSecTooltip: Longest interruption inside a block. 0 = 60 s (at least 2 polls).
finalRestValTooltip: Power below which the device counts as at rest after an early end. 0 = the standby threshold.
finalRestSecTooltip: Time at rest that ends the lock phase. 0 = 60 s (at least 3 polls).
finalActValTooltip: Power above which activity counts after an early end. 0 = off. Works only together with the activity share.
finalActShareTooltip: Share of the last 5 minutes above the activity level at which a new run is assumed (0.5 to 0.9). 0 = off, only together with the activity level.
finalCheckSecTooltip: Time after an early end in which the final band decides whether a new run started. 0 = 30 minutes.
finalLockSecTooltip: Longest lock phase after an early end (600 to 14400). 0 = 4 hours.
dm_learnRunsInfo: These are the runs found in the history of the last 30 days, with the result of the check (✓ = fine, otherwise the problem found). Usually you leave every run on "Auto" and press OK; then the learned values follow. "Auto" uses a run if the check allows it. "Use" also counts a run the check holds back, if you know it was a normal programme. "Do not use" leaves out a run that was not typical (a test, a cancelled programme, another load on the socket).
dm_learnFormerlyDropped: Some runs were not kept by the earlier learning data of this device. They are marked "formerly dropped"; check them before you use them.
dm_learnRecalcHelp: Shows this list again, checked for the runs you chose. Without it OK goes on to the suggestion.
dm_learnReviewRuns: Check the runs one by one first
dm_learnReviewRunsHelp: Only if needed: shows every run found and lets you choose which ones count. Without it the adapter decides on its own.
dm_learnFinalHelp: Reports the end as soon as the final part of the programme is over instead of after the long end time. Only offered when every check passed; off by default.
dm_finalReject_tooFewRuns: too few runs with a clear end
dm_finalReject_noSeparation: the final part cannot be told apart
dm_finalReject_tailInBand: the anti-crease phase reaches the final part
dm_finalReject_earlyEnd: a run would end too early
dm_finalReject_phantomStart: a run would be reported as started twice
dm_finalReject_worseOnFlagged: a run with findings gets worse
dm_learnPhasesHelp: Shows the phase of the device (for example "Final spin") in the states and lets you use it in actions and messages. The names can be changed.
dm_learnPhaseRetro: This phase is only recognised afterwards: it appears in the timeline but not live.
dm_learnChecks: Check of the recording: the values may be unreliable.
dm_optNewRun: The run after the early end was a new run
dm_optDropLegacyConfirm: Forget the limits taken over from the learning data of earlier versions? The limits then come from the stored runs alone, and a rare programme that is no longer stored may be reported as finished too early.
dm_optClearDecisions: Also discard my decisions about runs
